label: F-a87838

findings.note: QuotaReset.cs:20 and QuotaCooldowns.cs:10 do carry Source as a string checked against the QuotaSources constants, including a "none" sentinel. That is a fair doctrine point, but the plan's D4 itself names the values as wire strings, and nothing outside the code passes in arbitrary values.

KeyByFamily and BucketIdsByKey (AgyQuotaReport.cs:17-34) and NameByKey (QuotaCooldowns.cs:69) are separate tables, so a new key needs edits in up to three places. Adding a family to an existing key needs only one row, and a key with no bucket ids just falls back to stated/guess through HasGauge, so this is about maintainability, not a defect.
Judge at AgyQuotaReport.cs:118-125 does what the plan's D6 decided: "both active at 0 with one reset_time missing or past → Spent on the known one, the note naming the unknown", and S40 pins it.

The plan's S15 requires CannotCheck to name the first stderr line. The note is persisted only through VendorReason.Written, which is Redaction.SafeText (QuotaCooldowns.cs:212), so the file and the card get a redacted text, not raw stderr. Only the Information log at QuotaCooldownsRound.cs:64 carries it unredacted.

The probes do run one after another (QuotaCooldownsRound.cs:14-18), but only agy keys with a gauge probe (at most three, 30 s each), the plan accepts this cost (§8), and the probes are redundant since one /quota answer covers every group. That redundancy is the better fix.
The repo's CA1502 counting (.editorconfig:80-83) adds nothing for is/and patterns, so Fraction (AgyQuotaReport.cs:156-157) is 1 + && + ?: = 3, within the bound.
TryGroups (AgyQuotaReport.cs:131-139) is 1 + three && = 4, which is the allowed maximum, not over it.
Number (AgyQuotaReport.cs:160-163) is 1 + two && + ?: = 4, within the bound.

ReviewerInvocation (ReviewerRuntime.cs:214-223) has no launcher. The probe reuses invocation.Request, which carries the executable, environment and working directory, as D6 prescribes (AgyQuotaReport.cs:219-225).

The plan's D4 mandates HeldFile.TakeWithin with a 30 s wait, and the implementation deliberately moves that wait off the async caller with Task.Run (QuotaCooldownsRound.cs:28-29). One pool thread blocked once per round is not a thread-pool problem.

D5 says the gauge decides agy's undecided (Spent == null) case, so probing it is required. For other runtimes, the default ReadResetAsync (ReviewerRuntime.cs:+544) answers NoPark without launching anything.

At AgyError.cs:29-30, line.Length = lineEnd - from - leadingWhitespace, so lineEnd - line.Length = from + leadingWhitespace, which is exactly where the token starts. The slice is correct, and the next commit b45d1ea2 pins an indented CRLF line as passing.

At QuotaCooldownsRound.cs:29, Task.Run(() => Apply(changes)) has no guard, and TryCreateDataDir/Persisted catch only IOException and UnauthorizedAccessException, so an ArgumentException or NotSupportedException from an unusable data path escapes AfterRoundAsync. Commit b45d1ea2 fixes exactly this. It is an edge case, so major rather than blocking.
Usable's strict reset > nowUtc (AgyQuotaReport.cs:128-129) is the plan's D6 rule ("one whose reset_time is not after nowUtc — a past instant is no reset, never a park on the past").
D4 and S19 specify a warning "once per process", which is what WarnOnce does (QuotaCooldowns.cs:309-315).

AgyError.cs:30 does copy the rest of stderr for each AGY_ERROR line, but there is normally one such line on a failed launch's redacted stderr, so the cost is negligible and calling it quadratic overstates it.
Duplicate of index 4: the same sequential loop at QuotaCooldownsRound.cs:14-18, bounded at three 30 s probes for agy keys only.

Every key in BucketIdsByKey has at most two buckets (AgyQuotaReport.cs:29-34), so when usable.Count < spent.Count there is exactly one usable and one unusable bucket, and the note at line 125 names both.

missed: The read half of the same fail-open gap: Standing/TextOrNull (QuotaCooldowns.cs:249-265) catches only IOException and UnauthorizedAccessException, so an ArgumentException or NotSupportedException from an unusable data path escapes from PanelService.CanRun and ProbeAsync on every decision, breaking D4's fail-open contract (fixed with the write half in b45d1ea2).
Each spent agy key launches its own /quota probe even though one /quota answer carries every group, so a round with Gemini and 3p both spent runs agy twice for the same data.

The 'is not parked' Information log (QuotaCooldownsRound.cs:64) writes the CannotCheck text, which includes the probe's raw first stderr line, without going through VendorReason.Written, while the persisted note is redacted.
summary: Only one finding is a real defect worth fixing now: the unguarded Task.Run(Apply) can throw out of AfterRoundAsync. Most of the rest misread the code (the AGY_ERROR offset, the complexity counts, the launcher) or contradict decisions the plan made explicitly (the partial-reset rule, the strict 'after now' rule, warn-once, HeldFile), plus a few minor maintainability and latency points.
